tldr: A Sep 22 post asked how to evaluate agent memory beyond the context window. PACMI (Oct 5) then shifted the focus to keeping memory correct by invalidating stale entries.
whats_new: An open-source repo (Oct 11) stores coding-agent long-term memory as a tree of plain files, a simple alternative to a dedicated memory service.
why_it_matters: Agents that persist memory across sessions need an update and invalidation policy, not only a retrieval layer; plain-file stores make that state inspectable and diffable, but give you no invalidation for free.

status.detail: Memory work spans evaluation, invalidation research, and lightweight file-based implementations for coding agents.

beats.headline: A benchmark post asks how to evaluate memory beyond context windows
PACMI cascades invalidation through provenance-linked memories
beats.summary: Targets memories that become outdated as new observations arrive.

beats.headline: Coding-agent memory as a tree of plain files
beats.summary: An open-source repo implements long-term memory without a dedicated store.

open_questions: Does PACMI's invalidation cascade hold up on an independent long-horizon agent benchmark?
Will any file-based memory store publish results on stale-memory handling?
take_for_builders: If your agent persists memory across sessions, record where each memory came from and test that correcting one fact also retires memories derived from it, whatever the storage backend.
